# 0.2.0 published artifact attestation

[Русская версия](ru/0.2.0.md)

Historical release facts consolidated on 2026-11-08 from the local preparation
record before its retirement. Git object types and public GitHub Release metadata
were independently checked during that review; the old runtime/security tests
were not rerun. This record does not alter the tagged notes or published assets.

## Preparation and recovery

An earlier build-only run `30015920014` produced SHA-256
`0120ee8125265585e07354b679f7aaacff0a6f59dd75b485a07b74e8fcb96028`, build time
`2026-07-23T14:28:09.972Z`. It is not the published binary. Different build
timestamps explain the difference; no byte replacement occurred between the
successful release workflow build, its draft and public publication.

The initial [tag-triggered run 30016595086](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/actions/runs/30016595086)
failed closed before creating a draft/assets because checkout had represented
the local tag ref by its peeled commit. The remote annotated tag was intact.
Recovery tooling commit `7f443b1bf63432cd1dbabb88fa56e060ae7f1bab` fetched the remote
tag into a private validation ref; contract tests covered that distinction.
[CI 30017275118](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/actions/runs/30017275118)
and [release recovery 30017393026](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/actions/runs/30017393026)
passed. Recovery tooling ran from `main`, while source, notes, build and packaging
contracts remained selected from immutable `v0.2.0`. The tag was never moved or
recreated. The downloaded workflow artifact and draft/public JAR were recorded
byte-identical with matching sidecar and embedded source identity.

## Qualification boundary

[Dependency Security 30015917073](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/actions/runs/30015917073)
recorded Dependency-Check 12.2.2, NVD last-checked `2026-07-23T14:28:59Z`,
128 dependencies and no vulnerable dependencies for this candidate. This is a
dated result, not present-day dependency assurance.

Dependabot alert `#104` / `GHSA-5gvw-p9qm-jgwh` had a separate human
applicability disposition. `tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind:3.1.4` was
present through Spring Boot 4.0.7, so it was not a false positive. The recorded
advisory condition required view-based deserialization with both `@JsonView`
and `@JsonUnwrapped` on a container property. The candidate search found neither
annotation nor `readerWithView`/`withView`; its supported HTTP surface was
loopback Actuator. The alert was dismissed as `not_used`, corresponding to
project disposition `not_applicable`. The recorded review triggers were adding
those annotations/view-based deserialization, a public write API, or changing
the Jackson/Boot graph. Maintenance upgrade to 3.1.5+ was deferred after release.
This candidate-specific decision is separate from the Dependency-Check result
and must not be reused for later versions or the open 0.3.0 SRC-3 screen.

The idle-stand rollback sequence `02f0750 → 58ab1e7 → 02f0750` retained dataframe/
service schemas `3/7`, four ingest runs, and counts masks=60, ip_list=26,
address_blacklist=86, hashes=129. Health was UP and no restarts/errors were
recorded. There were no storage/schema changes between those binaries, so this
application rollback did not restore databases. It does not authorize binary-only
rollback across later schema changes.

SMB fetch/publish/reconcile smoke was explicitly skipped: `sync.enabled=false`
and no test endpoint was provisioned. It was not a completed remote gate.
